message.content:
Yes—Atlanta residents can file a noise‑complaint with the city’s local authorities.  
In Atlanta, noise complaints are typically handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** or the **City of Atlanta Office of the City Clerk** (which oversees the City Council).  

### How to file a complaint

| Step | What to do | Where to go |
|------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Call 311** (or dial 911 if the noise is an emergency). | 311 (non‑emergency) or 911 (emergency) |
| 2 | **Use the online portal**: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> | Online form or chat |
| 3 | **Visit the City Clerk’s office**: 1000 Peachtree Street NE, Atlanta, GA 30308 | In‑person or by mail |
| 4 | **Contact the Police Department**: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/police> | 311 or 911 for immediate response |

### What information you’ll need

- **Date & time** of the noise
- **Location** (address or intersection)
- **Description** of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs)
- **Any evidence** (photos, videos, audio recordings)

### Relevant law

Atlanta’s noise ordinance is part of the city’s **Local Law 2015‑1** (Noise Regulation). The ordinance sets permissible noise levels and defines prohibited activities. You can find the full text on the city’s website under “Local Laws” or “Noise Ordinance.”

---

**Quick tip:** If you’re unsure whether the noise violates the ordinance, the City Clerk’s office can help interpret the law and advise on next steps.
